title: Loaded Nacho Skillet
shortDescription: Game-night skillet the whole hall shares
subtitle: Game-night skillet the whole hall shares
description: Game-night skillet the whole hall shares. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Brown beef and onion
steps.instruction: In a 12-inch cast iron skillet over medium-high, brown ground beef with diced onion until no pink remains. Drain grease. Add taco seasoning and ⅓ cup water; simmer until thick.

steps.title: Layer chips and cheese
steps.instruction: Off heat, scatter tortilla chips over the beef in the skillet. Top with black beans, shredded cheddar, and jalapeños.

steps.title: Bake until bubbling
steps.instruction: Bake at 425°F 8–10 minutes until cheese is fully melted and edges bubble. Watch the broiler side — cast iron holds heat and can burn chip edges fast.

steps.title: Serve from the skillet
steps.instruction: Set the hot skillet on a trivet at the table with sour cream and salsa on the side. Loaded Nacho Skillet is communal — provide a big spoon and expect fingers.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Label every topping bowl — rookies grab faster when they can read the line.
Keep hot bases (potatoes, chips) in cambros at 200°F and cold toppings on ice if service runs long.
Put forks, napkins, and a trash can at the end of the bar — self-serve feeds get messy fast.

leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
